title: Fabric Spark autoscale internals
purpose: Decision cycle for dynamic allocation: initial reserve, demand-led growth, bounded scale-up, idle detection, and safe executor decommission with shuffle risk.
accessibleSummary: Fabric Spark autoscale internals. Spark job demand; Minimum executor reserve; Tasks exceed capacity?; Scale toward maximum; Idle executors detected?; Decommission safely; Shuffle blocks pin workers.
longDescription: Decision cycle for dynamic allocation: initial reserve, demand-led growth, bounded scale-up, idle detection, and safe executor decommission with shuffle risk.

nodes.label: Spark job demand
nodes.summary: A notebook or Spark Job Definition submits work against a configured pool.
nodes.detail: Job shape and concurrency establish useful executor demand.

evidence.note: Fabric runs notebooks and jobs on managed starter or custom Spark pools.

drill.example: A nightly transform submits to a custom autoscale pool.

nodes.label: Minimum executor reserve
nodes.summary: Dynamic allocation reserves executors from the pool minimum at submission.
nodes.detail: The minimum provides the starting worker envelope.

evidence.note: Dynamic allocation initially reserves executors based on the pool minimum.

drill.example: Two workers start a small ingestion stage.

nodes.label: Tasks exceed capacity?
nodes.summary: Dynamic allocation grows executors when runnable tasks outstrip capacity.
nodes.detail: Runtime demand is compared with available executor slots.
nodes.whyItMatters: Wide and narrow stages scale differently.

evidence.note: Executor count grows when tasks exceed capacity and shrinks when work completes or idles.

drill.example: A wide join requests more workers.
failureModes: Skew leaves one long task that cannot use more executors.

nodes.label: Scale toward maximum
nodes.summary: The pool adds workers only within its configured maximum.
nodes.detail: Scale-up expands parallelism without exceeding the administrative ceiling.
nodes.whyItMatters: The maximum is a guardrail, not an efficiency promise.

evidence.note: Autoscale operates between configured minimum and maximum node counts.

drill.example: A join grows from two to eight workers.

nodes.label: Idle executors detected?
nodes.summary: Executors become release candidates after work completes or idles.
nodes.detail: Scale-down evaluates unused workers while preserving correctness.

evidence.note: Dynamic allocation releases executors as work completes or the application idles.

drill.example: A narrow write no longer needs eight workers.

nodes.label: Decommission safely
nodes.summary: Fabric enables executor decommission by default for automatic scale-down.
nodes.detail: Eligible workers leave while required application state is protected.

drill.example: Six workers leave after their work completes.
failureModes: Disabling it makes scale-down less aggressive.

nodes.label: Shuffle blocks pin workers
nodes.summary: Local shuffle data can prevent release until downstream readers finish.
nodes.detail: This warning explains low CPU with a cluster that will not shrink.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle diagnosis prevents false autoscale conclusions.

evidence.note: Local shuffle storage can keep executors alive until downstream stages consume their blocks.

processing: Wait for reads or use supported shuffle handling
drill.example: A worker remains through a downstream aggregation.
failureModes: Executor loss causes FetchFailedException and recomputation.
